newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage rates fall in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage rates fall in latest week.

text.p: Mortgages rates moved slightly lower in the week ending April 11, Freddie Mac said Thursday, as bond markets calmed down after the Federal Reserve's recent increase in interest rates.
Freddie Mac said rates for 30-year loans fell to an average 8.15 percent from 8.18 percent last week, while 15-year mortgages dipped to 7.67 percent from 7.70 percent.
One-year adjustable rate mortgages rose in the week to 5.91 percent from 5.80 percent, it said.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 8.05 percent, the 15-year 7.56 percent and the ARM 5.80 percent.
"Long-term interest rates seem to have settled down since the Federal Reserve raised short-term rates a few weeks ago," Robert Van Order, Freddie Mac chief economist, said.
"We probably won't see much movement in these figures now until release of the next employment report or the Consumer Price Index," Van Order added.

Lenders charged an average 1.8 percent in fees and points on both 30- and 15-year loans, up from 1.7 percent last week. They charged 1.5 percent on adjustable loans, up from 1.4 percent from last week.
Freddie Mac is a corporation chartered by Congress that buys mortgages from lenders and packages them into securities for investors.
